newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power prices hold fairly steady.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power prices hold fairly steady.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. held relatively steady Wednesday ahead of forecasts of below normal temperatures through the weekend and early next week, industry sources said.

Temperatures through the Mid-West were predicted to be below and much below normal from January 12 to 16, although forecasts called for temperatures near normal levels through much of the area later from January 17 to 21.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were discussed steady in the $23.00-25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next day non-firm MAPP power was said to be off slightly in the $10.50-12.00 range from $11.00-12.50 on Tuesday, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday fell to $23.25-24.25 from $25.00-27.50 on Tuesday.
MAIN off peak next day power was assessed lower at $13.00-15.00 from $14.00-16.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday were talked in the $28.00-30.00 range in the north and northeast of the region from a $26.00-28.00 range on Tuesday.
Also in ECAR, prices at Cinergy for Thursday delivery were pegged at $22.25-23.25 from $21.50-23.00 per MWh on Tuesday.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were quoted steady at $12.00-14.00, the sources said.
One trader reported selling peak ECAR power for the five business days of next week at $25.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was notionally assessed stronger at $28.25-28.65 from $24.00-24.50 per MWh on Tuesday.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery climbed into the $25.00-26.00 area from $23.00-24.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP for Thursday delivery were notionally assessed steady at $12.50-13.50 per MWh.
February SPP was said to have eased to $23.50-24.50 from $24.50-25.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Separately, Detroit Edison's 1,116 megawatt (MW) Fermi 2 nuclear unit in Michigan was expected to synchronize to the grid Wednesday after the company interrupted restart operations on Monday.
Also, the 1,205 megawatt (MW) Perry nuclear power plant in North Perry, Ohio, was scheduled to startup later Wednesday after tripping off line Tuesday due to an electrical problem, the operator said.

Northern Indiana Public Service Co said Wednesday that coal unit 18 at its Schahfer generating station, shut Friday for scheduled maintenance, will be down for about seven weeks. The unit, in northwest Indiana, has a generating capacity of 361 megawatts.
